Content:
To divide a whole number by a unit fraction, we multiply the whole number by the fraction's denominator.

Content:
For example,

Content:
[MATH: {\color{red}{2}}\div \dfrac 1{\color{blue}{3}} = {\color{red}{2}}\times {\color{blue}{3}} = 6.]

Content:
Now, note the following:

Content:
- [MATH: {\color{blue}{3}}] is the reciprocal of [MATH: \dfrac1{\color{blue}{3}}.]
- So, to calculate [MATH: {\color{red}{2}}\div \dfrac 1{\color{blue}{3}},] we multiplied [MATH: \color{red}2] by the reciprocal of [MATH: \dfrac1{\color{blue}{3}}.]

Content:
Thinking about division in terms of reciprocals will help us later when we want to divide whole numbers by non-unit fractions.

items.readable_text:
Content:
When dividing a whole number by a non-unit fraction, we can still use the same technique of multiplying the whole number by the reciprocal of the fraction.

Content:
The only difference is that, in order to perform the multiplication, we must convert the whole number into an improper fraction.

Content:
To illustrate, let's compute [MATH: 3\div \dfrac 2 9 .]

Content:
First, we write [MATH: 3] as an improper fraction:

Content:
[MATH: 3=\dfrac{3}{1}]

Content:
Next, we note that the reciprocal of [MATH: \dfrac{\color{blue}2}{\color{red}9}] is [MATH: \dfrac{\color{red}9}{\color{blue}2} .]

Content:
So, we have

Content:
[MATH: 3\div \dfrac 2 9 =

\dfrac 3 1 \div \dfrac{\color{blue}2}{\color{red}9} = \dfrac 3 1 \times \dfrac{\color{red}9}{\color{blue}2}.]

Content:
Now, we multiply our fractions.

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac 3 {1} \times \dfrac{9}{2} = \dfrac {3\times 9} {1\times 2} = \dfrac{27}{2}]

sections.normalized_html: Calculate the value of [MATH: 4\div \dfrac35,] expressing the result as a mixed number.
sections.readable_text: Calculate the value of [MATH: 4\div \dfrac35,] expressing the result as a mixed number.

sections.normalized_html:
Dividing a whole number by a fraction is equivalent to multiplying the whole number by the reciprocal of the fraction.

First, we write [MATH: 4] as an improper fraction:

[MATH: 4=\dfrac{4}{1}]

Next, we note that the reciprocal of [MATH: \dfrac{\color{blue}3}{\color{red}5}] is [MATH: \dfrac{\color{red}5}{\color{blue}3}.]

So, we have

[MATH: 4\div \dfrac 3 5 = \dfrac 4 1 \div \dfrac{\color{blue}3}{\color{red}5} = \dfrac 4 1 \times \dfrac{\color{red}5}{\color{blue}3}.]

Now, we multiply our fractions.

[MATH: \dfrac 4 {1} \times \dfrac{5}{3} = \dfrac {4\times 5} {1\times 3} = \dfrac{20}{3}]

Finally, we write the resulting improper fraction as a mixed number:

[MATH: \dfrac{20}{3} =6\,\textrm{R} 2 = 6\,\dfrac 2 {3}]

Content:
Let's find the value of [MATH: 8\div \dfrac 4 5.]

Content:
Dividing a whole number by a fraction is equivalent to multiplying the whole number by the reciprocal of the fraction.

Content:
First, we write [MATH: 8] as an improper fraction:

Content:
[MATH: 8=\dfrac{8}{1}]

Content:
Next, we note that the reciprocal of [MATH: \dfrac{\color{blue}4}{\color{red}5}] is [MATH: \dfrac{\color{red}5}{\color{blue}4}.]

Content:
So, we have

Content:
[MATH: 8\div \dfrac 4 5 =
\dfrac 8 1 \div \dfrac{\color{blue}4}{\color{red}5} = \dfrac 8 1 \times \dfrac{\color{red}5}{\color{blue}4}.]

Content:
Now, we multiply our fractions.

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac 8 {1} \times \dfrac{5}{4} = \dfrac {8\times 5} {1\times 4} = \dfrac{40}{4}]

Content:
Finally, we simplify:

Content:
[MATH: 40 \div 4 = 10.]

Content:
Sometimes, we may wish to use a fraction multiplication strategy to simplify the problem before multiplying the fractions. Let's see an example.

sections.normalized_html:
Dividing a whole number by a fraction is equivalent to multiplying the whole number by the reciprocal of the fraction.

First, we write [MATH: 8] as an improper fraction:

[MATH: 8=\dfrac{8}{1}]

Next, we note that the reciprocal of [MATH: \dfrac{\color{blue}2}{\color{red}5}] is [MATH: \dfrac{\color{red}5}{\color{blue}2}.]

So, we have

[MATH: 8\div \dfrac 2 5 = \dfrac {8} 1 \div \dfrac{\color{blue}2}{\color{red}5} = \dfrac {8} 1 \times \dfrac{\color{red}5}{\color{blue}2}.]

Now, we multiply our fractions. Note that we can simplify the process by swapping the denominators first.

[MATH: (8)/(1) × (5)/(2)|= (8)/(2) × (5)/(1); = 4 × 5; = 20]
